why: Same expert geometry (512 experts, top-10, CPU experts, NVMe streaming, batch 1) so it is the closest published regime. But (a) only 33 GB model squeezed to 24-32 GB RAM, we have 69 GB vs 8-32 GB; (b) most of the end-to-end gain is the explicit-read prefetcher (1.31x/1.52x) and the interleave, not the co-activation reorder (1.05x over prefetcher, 1.08x at 32 GB); (c) layout is invisible to mmap faults; (d) self-reported, one machine, N=3, 8 stars; (e) the author states profile-free coalescing carries ~90% of the win and the clique reorder adds ~12% of read ops at decode, and that plain LRU beats any pinned set and cross-layer prefetch is a null.
quality_loss: Weights byte-exact; routing equivalence 100.000% through the permutation at equal inputs; KLD 0.00096 and top-1 agreement 98.9% (5x below CPU vs Metal backend delta) per README; author notes token-identity is impossible under any expert permutation (floating-point sum order). No benchmark scores.
ablation: Yes and it isolates what we need: stock+pf 7.60, reorder+pf 8.00, interleave+pf 9.00, interleave without pf 5.70 (README, phase2). Phase 0 replay ablation: heat 1.06, pipeline 1.07, clique 1.11, chain 1.14, clique+pipeline 1.23, chain+pipeline 1.23, interleave 1.59 (warm 32/128).
limitations: Authors state: gains scale with I/O-boundness (model >= RAM); layout only pays with explicit reads (mmap parity measured); big ~4 MB slices cap per-read gain at ~1.3x; moderate ratios with big slices weak (~+10%); LRU-caching engines see +14-18% not the no-retention numbers; trace should resemble deployment (matched tracing worth ~20-30%); single machine; baseline varied between sessions (5.8 vs 10.0 across days, within-session ratios only); interleave is CPU-experts only.
contradicts_our_findings: No. It confirms them: our leave-one-out reorder gain 1.045x serial / 1.073x overlapped at 8 GB, 1.003x at 16 GB and 1.000x at 32 GB (pubtech/C.md) matches mbolt's 1.053x over the prefetcher and 1.077x at 32 GB squeeze; our held-out run length 1.35 on 128-expert traces; mbolt's own simulator over-predicted (modeled 1.10x, replay 1.23x, real e2e 1.05x). What changes: the large lever is the contiguous per-expert interleave (our family #19 repack), 2.23x I/O and 1.18x e2e over the prefetcher; do not credit it to co-activation reorder.

title: LLM in a flash: Efficient Large Language Model Inference with Limited Memory (Keivan Alizadeh, Iman Mirzadeh, Dmitry Belenko, S. Karen Khatamifard, Minsik Cho, Carlo C Del Mundo, Mohammad Rastegari, Mehrdad Farajtabar; Apple; ACL 2024)
id_read: arXiv:2312.11514v3 [cs.CL] 30 Jul 2024, PDF via pdftotext (139,904 chars)
setup: OPT 6.7B (ReLU), sparsified Falcon 7B, Phi-2, Persimmon 8B, Llama 2 7B (FATReLU); dense FFN neurons, no experts. Hardware: Apple M1 Max 1 TB SSD, Apple M2 Ultra 2 TB SSD (CPU float32 or Metal float16), Linux box with RTX 4090 24 GB (bf16). About half of the model allowed in DRAM. Flash throughput: 6.10 GB/s dense sequential, 1.25 GB/s sparse reads, 2.25 GB/s with bundling; 32 reader threads; reads without OS caching (purge). Data: C4 validation, 128-token prompt, 256 generated tokens. Baselines: naive (reload on demand, best theoretical I/O numbers used, 'real number might be higher') and hybrid (half in DRAM, half loaded). Software: HF Transformers + PyTorch + custom binary extension.

why: Dense ReLU-sparse FFN neurons (predictor decides which neurons), not top-k routed experts; DRAM holds half the model plus a sliding window of recently active neurons, while we have 8-32 GB against 69 GB; baselines are best-case theory, not llama.cpp; Apple SSD with 32 parallel readers. The only transferable pieces are the chunk-size/throughput curve (1.25 -> 2.25 GB/s when chunk doubles), which matches our 0.9 MB -> 4 MiB curve idea, and the negative co-activation-bundling result (qualitative).

ablation: Yes (Table 2, cumulative: hybrid, predictor, windowing, bundling) but bundling only in its row-column form; co-activation bundling has no numbers.
limitations: Authors: only half of model in DRAM tested; relies on ReLU sparsity (relufied models for Falcon, Phi-2, Llama2); baselines use theoretical best I/O ('real number might be higher'); needs predictors; they note OS buffer cache could improve figures; Metal needs custom extension for dynamic shapes.
contradicts_our_findings: No. Consistent with our held-out co-activation reorder being weak (pubtech/C.md family #20). Their row-column bundling is the analogue of our gate/up/down repack (family #19), not of reorder.

why: A100 GPU with PCIe from host DRAM; benefit is overlapping 16 GB/s PCIe transfers with draft compute; needs a GPU-resident quantized draft copy of the same model plus FP16 target; 8-64 experts; CPU-only, 8-32 GB RAM, NVMe streaming break all assumptions. Bytes read are not reduced, and our simulation (pubtech/C.md #21) shows verify-union bytes ratio >= 1 for K>=2.

limitations: v3: Phi-3.5 hides only 22.4% of H2D; gains shrink when LRU-S has big cache (32 GB); batch growth increases expert working set (Fig.16); depends on high draft-target alignment. v1: cannot compare to vLLM/llama.cpp directly (built on Transformers); no small same-architecture MoE draft exists so draft ablation 'cannot be conducted'.
contradicts_our_findings: No. Matches pubtech/C.md #21: draft-based gain is prefetch overlap, not fewer bytes. Table 6 shows oracle prefetch is only 1.34x better than 41%-accurate prefetch, i.e. on a GPU-PCIe system prediction quality has limited upside; in a disk-bound CPU system with prefetch window of one layer compute (~ms) vs read time the overlap budget is far smaller.

it is Table III 'Top-k = all routed experts correct' (for Qwen3/DeepSeek that is top-8, 55-61%), table numbering III; range 54.16-66.85% correct
plus 128 GB RAM, PCIe 4.0

why: GPU with PCIe from host RAM; Mixtral top-2 of 8 makes 'dense prefill' trivially true; for decode, the predictor needs per-layer GPU inference and trace training (<=9 h) and only prefetches, so CPU-only NVMe streaming loses the GPU compute overlap; no disk.
quality_loss: None claimed (prefetch/cache only, quantization is AWQ/FP8 from the model setup).
ablation: Limited: compares to ODF, LFP, MIF; no phase-by-phase ablation of prefill vs decode components found in text; predictor accuracy compared in Table III.
limitations: Authors: models with larger expert pools and sparser routing are harder to learn; throughput gain shrinks at large batch; MIF OOMs on 22B; predictor training needs offline traces.
contradicts_our_findings: No, but it does not support 'prefill touches nearly every expert' for 128+ expert models; our decode-trace coverage 55-66% after 200 tokens (proxy) leaves that open. Absolute baseline latencies are in figures (not text-extractable).
